I'm a statistician who builds interpretable models for messy observational data, along with the software to run them reliably at scale.

At the [Natural History Museum](https://www.nhm.ac.uk/) in London, I lead the modelling and engineering behind the [Biodiversity Intactness Index](https://www.nhm.ac.uk/our-science/services/data/biodiversity-intactness-index.html). This involves hierarchical mixed-effects models fitted to heterogeneous data pooled from many independent field studies, then projected globally.

Before that, I did a PhD in statistics at the [University of Western Australia](https://www.uwa.edu.au/) and a postdoc at the [University of Cambridge](https://www.cam.ac.uk/), developing Bayesian methods for combining mechanistic models with data when those models are known to be wrong ([PNAS, 2021](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2015006118)).
